records.swap_audit:
==== SWAP AUDIT — why each detected face was or was not swapped ====
  faces seen                                                         1133  100.0%
    of those, crop shared with the face beside it                     320   28.2%
    of those, gap-filled                                              302   26.7%
  swapped (identity lock)                                             490   43.2%
  no track entry matched                                              464   41.0%
  fallback missed (this person's source already used this frame)      241   21.3%
  fallback missed (over match threshold)                              223   19.7%
  veto: source used twice in frame                                    179   15.8%
  refused: crop shared with the face beside it                        163   14.4%
  swapped (per-frame match)                                            16    1.4%
    of those, partly behind an object (masked, still swapped)         281   24.8%
    of those SWAPPED, gap-filled                                       93    8.2%
  discarded: the swap put the face somewhere it was not                 7    0.6%
  -> 634 of 1133 detected faces (56.0%) were NOT swapped.
     7 of those were swapped and then DISCARDED by the outcome check, which pastes the original face back — a refusal like any other as far as the output is concerned. ROOP_VERIFY_SWAP=0 turns it off.
     Frames where a face was found but left un-swapped are what reads as flicker. The largest refusal line above is the gate to loosen.
     93 of the 506 faces actually swapped (18.4%) had INTERPOLATED landmarks — nobody detected them, their box and keypoints were filled in between neighbours.
     That is a different artefact from the one above: the swap is not missing, it is registered from a guess, so on a moving head it shifts every other frame. Set ROOP_TEMPORAL_STEP=1 if this is high.
     Of those, 223 were refused for distance alone, and this is how far past the match threshold (0.75) their BEST candidate sat:
       within 1.05x the threshold (0.79):       5  (  2.2% of them)
       within 1.10x the threshold (0.83):      13  (  5.8% of them)
       within 1.20x the threshold (0.90):     161  ( 72.2% of them)
       within 1.50x the threshold (1.12):     223  (100.0% of them)
       within 2.00x the threshold (1.50):     223  (100.0% of them)
       median refusal sits at 1.17x the threshold (0.88).
     Separately, 37 frames of 744 (5.0% of frames) had NO face detected at all — that is the detector losing the face, not a gate refusing it, so it is a different problem from every refusal above.
     (no detector scores recorded — only retinaface reports them; on another engine, compare engines or raise the detector resolution.)
     Separately, 1 detections were dropped as the JUNCTION between two touching faces rather than a face — half of each neighbour, which the detector reports at up to 0.99 confidence. ROOP_FACE_MERGE=0 keeps them.
